title: Ben's rifle and bow, and the Bellevue incident
summary: Ben takes up a Winchester and bow and arrows, and in New York he is taken to Bellevue for sighting a rifle from his Harlem window until Sid Catlett gets him released.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: I finished the engagement through the courtesy of Gilby's gin and some codeine for the pain at night. Oh yes, just about then, Ben bought a beautiful 30-30 Winchester 94, and kept it off with a fine bow and quiver of arrows. He lost his riding companion (me) so we still went out to the stables, and still riding -- we'd target practice with a rifle and bow. Our targets -- huge piles of manure and rats at the trash dump.

Ben was sighting his rifle while cleaning it out of the fourth floor apartment in Harlem, in New York, and somebody noticed him and called the police, and they took Ben to Bellevue for evaluation. Sidney Catlett, Ben's dear friend, went down to get him out. The psychiatrist, a lady -- the psychiatrist was a lady, and she was buttered up by Sidney, telling her it was all a big mistake, and all about Ben's virtues. She called Ben in and asked him what in the world he was doing in the city with his sporting equipment, and Ben replied, 'I was just trying my bow and arrows out!'

It took more sweetness on Catlett's part to get him released in his custody. So you see, whoever may study these tapes to further his career, must understand a musician can have his recreation and create beautiful sounds at the same time. I miss the sounds of and the playing with Ben Webster, may God watch over his merry soul in heaven, and to cap off the Ben Cassy saga, I would say that as we ride off BENGAZI
into the sunset, I'm an old cowhand from the Webster band! (Sings)
Hey George, that was quite some saga. That Ben Gassy saga from the Washington era, you being a horseman and all -- sorry about that horse and you!
